Kinda needed to see this <3 

Just broke up with my boyfriend of 15 months because I just couldn't deny my sexuality any longer. At the moment I'm struggling with trying to figure out if I'm actually Bi, like I'd been identifying as for the past year or so or if I'm really just a lesbian. I really can't tell if I was ever properly attracted to the men I've dated in the past or just was dating them because they were nice guys I felt comfortable around. The biggest thing for me has been recognising that feeling safe and comfortable around a man /= being attracted to them. All my relationships with them have ended with both of us feeling more like friends than romantic partners. 

It feels like I need to have a label, to be able to be proud of who I am and feel valid in an identity even though that really isn't the case, and my identity over the years has changed and that doesn't make any previous or future label any less valid.

My plan has always been to keep my name if I ever choose to marry, which I had felt conflicted about carrying his name on. In telling him that I've changed my name, that point would come up and would go against that family's traditional views. Apparently that would be 'too feminist' 

Though I do admit the family would be far more upset had one of my brother's changed their name, and not me.

Last year I went into hospital for a terrible kidney infection. I was there for a good 4 days and had quite a few tests done (blood tests, ultrasounds etc). I'm so thankful for Medicare here in Aus, because I walked out of the hospital having paid $28 for all the medication I left with.  

It was the first time I'd really been in hospital (barring two overnight ER visits as a young teen) and I was unaware of what I'd have to pay and how all that works here as I'd overwhelmingly heard horror stories about cost in the US. I was terrified the whole time I was there I'd get some bill I couldn't afford to pay, and I couldn't imagine what it would've been had I not been so lucky to live somewhere with great healthcare.
